1.key: Now, the way the cash cycle works in a business like AWS is that you have to spend the cash for data centers, servers and networking gear well in advance of when you can monetize it.

subs.en: Now, the way the cash cycle works in a business like AWS is that you have to spend the cash for data centers, servers and networking gear well in advance of when you can monetize it.
subs.ko: AWS 같은 사업에서 현금이 도는 방식은, 데이터센터와 서버·네트워크 장비에 돈을 버는 시점보다 한참 먼저 써야 한다는 겁니다.

subs.en: So when you're growing at this unprecedented rate, you end up having a lot of capex, which creates some headwinds on your short-term free cash flow,
subs.ko: 그래서 전례 없는 속도로 크면, 설비투자가 많아지고 단기 잉여현금흐름에는 역풍이 됩니다.

subs.en: but the economics of the business are such that once you get a few years out, with the data centers installed and monetizing the servers and gear in place, you really like the free cash flow and the return on invested capital.
subs.ko: 하지만 몇 년 지나 데이터센터가 다 들어서고 서버와 장비로 돈을 벌기 시작하면, 잉여현금흐름과 투하자본수익률이 아주 좋아지는 사업입니다.

subs.en: And I think we're going to be a much larger company, and AWS a much larger business than we ever anticipated.
subs.ko: 그리고 아마존은 훨씬 큰 회사가, AWS는 저희가 생각했던 것보다 훨씬 큰 사업이 될 겁니다.

subs.en: We felt AWS could be a few hundred billion-dollar revenue run-rate business. We now believe it can be over a trillion dollars in the next five to ten years.
subs.ko: AWS가 연 매출 수천억 달러 사업이 될 수 있다고 봤는데, 이제는 5~10년 안에 1조 달러를 넘을 수 있다고 봅니다.

2.heard: And would it be more convenient if this type of acceleration and opportunity happened over 25 years,

2.key: and you could spread the capex over 25 years
2.heard: and you could spread the cat -backs over 25 years?
2.ko: 설비투자를 25년에 나눠 쓸 수 있다면 더 편하겠냐고요?

2.key: yeah it might be more convenient … that's not the opportunity
2.heard: Yeah, it might be more convenient, but that's not the world that we live in, and that's not the opportunity.
2.ko: 네, 더 편할지도 모르죠. 하지만 그건 우리가 사는 세상이 아니고, 이 기회도 그렇지 않습니다.

2.heard: And we can fund this plan,
2.ko: 우리는 이 계획에 돈을 댈 수 있습니다.

35.key: Well, it's not considered to be amongst the strongest. It's not a hyperscaler, so to speak. So what it's showing you is that the bond market is willing to impose discipline on borrowers that may have cash flow that's less clear to them.

subs.en: Well, it's not considered to be amongst the strongest. It's not a hyperscaler, so to speak. So what it's showing you is that the bond market is willing to impose discipline on borrowers that may have cash flow that's less clear to them.
subs.ko: 코어위브는 가장 튼튼한 쪽으로 여겨지지 않습니다. 이른바 하이퍼스케일러가 아니죠. 그러니 이건, 현금흐름이 덜 분명한 차입자에게 채권시장이 규율을 들이댈 준비가 돼 있다는 걸 보여 줍니다.

subs.en: So it may not apply simply to lower-rated companies. It can eventually apply to high-rated nations. Look at France — considered much better as a credit, but with a very high budget deficit, and the bond market is beginning to impose discipline on it.
subs.ko: 신용등급 낮은 회사에만 해당하는 것도 아닙니다. 결국 등급 높은 나라에도 해당될 수 있어요. 프랑스를 보세요. 신용은 훨씬 좋다지만 재정적자가 커서, 채권시장이 규율을 들이대기 시작했습니다.

subs.en: It did so in 2022 when Liz Truss attempted to raise the budget deficit. The bond market said no, and the 10-year yield rose 150 basis points in a few weeks — dramatic for a government bond market. So the CoreWeave story can be applied to all bonds.
subs.ko: 2022년 리즈 트러스 총리가 재정적자를 늘리려 하자 채권시장이 안 된다고 했고, 10년물 금리가 몇 주 만에 1.5%포인트 뛰었습니다. 국채시장에선 극적인 일이죠. 그러니 코어위브 이야기는 모든 채권에 적용될 수 있습니다.

5.key: My view is it's always an incredible year for the bond market. But I think this is an unusual time, because it's really the year when the AI boom became debt-financed.

subs.en: My view is it's always an incredible year for the bond market. But I think this is an unusual time, because it's really the year when the AI boom became debt-financed.
subs.ko: 채권시장은 늘 대단한 해라고 보지만, 올해는 특별합니다. AI 호황이 빚으로 굴러가기 시작한 해거든요.

subs.en: It used to be financed primarily by the huge, prodigious free cash flows of these companies — incredible companies with incredible products.
subs.ko: 전에는 주로 이 회사들의 어마어마한 잉여현금으로 돈을 댔습니다. 대단한 제품을 가진 대단한 회사들이죠.

subs.en: But this year they're kind of tapped out of that, and are turning to the bond market, to securitization, to private credit.
subs.ko: 그런데 올해는 그 돈을 거의 다 써서, 채권시장으로, 유동화로, 사모 대출로 가고 있습니다.

subs.en: I think if this does break bad at some point, we're going to look at 2026 as the year when it started.
subs.ko: 언젠가 이게 나빠진다면, 2026년을 그 시작으로 돌아보게 될 겁니다.

18.ko: 리스라는 형태의 금융이 있고, 우리는 그걸 수단으로 써 왔습니다.

18.heard: we're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, um, given that, uh, where our rates ratings are and, and sort of, we haven't been able to, and we haven't yet, I would say, uh, tap that.
18.ko: 신용등급 덕분에 채권시장에도 접근할 수 있는데, 아직은, 말하자면, 쓰지 않았습니다.

32.key: I think it'll be interesting over time whether all the different players who are building data centers have a broad enough business, with enough services, to build long-term sustainable businesses. We'll have to see.

subs.en: I think it'll be interesting over time whether all the different players who are building data centers have a broad enough business, with enough services, to build long-term sustainable businesses. We'll have to see.
subs.ko: 데이터센터를 짓는 여러 회사가 오래 버틸 사업을 만들 만큼 넓은 사업과 서비스를 가졌는지는, 시간이 지나 봐야 알 겁니다. 지켜봐야죠.

subs.en: It is growing so fast — I can understand why a lot of people are interested in it.
subs.ko: 워낙 빨리 크니까, 많은 사람이 뛰어드는 이유는 이해합니다.
